# PostureCheckMultiProcess

PostureCheckMultiProcess is a Ziti posture check that a device passes while the listed processes run on it: all of them or any one, as the semantic says.

| | |
|---|---|
| API version | `ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Namespaced |
| In Ziti | posture check of type `PROCESS_MULTI`, `/edge/management/v1/posture-checks` |
| Updated with | `PATCH`: a setting that is left out of the spec is left alone in Ziti |

## Example

From [`examples/posturecheck/multiprocess.yaml`](../../examples/posturecheck/multiprocess.yaml):

```yaml
apiVersion: ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: PostureCheckMultiProcess
metadata:
  name: endpoint-agents
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    kind: ProviderConfig
    name: default
  forProvider:
    name: endpoint-agents
    # AnyOf: one of the processes must be running. AllOf: all of them.
    semantic: AnyOf
    # A pair of operating system and path may be listed once.
    processes:
      - osType: macOS
        path: /Library/Endpoint Agent/agent
        signerFingerprints:
          - "F5:B9:8B:6F:B4:46:F0:74:38:F2:FA:72:F5:5D:60:ED:D8:B7:E3:61"
      - osType: Linux
        path: /opt/endpoint-agent/bin/agent
        hashes:
          - "a7fe5c886fad6bc932ada51ac4d35faa43a2f0a29bfd3122e1b28c1d4a1e4e5f33eb5f61b21ffe12994411445e855563266ff093d853279acc240ee426d60ab3"
          - "085B1D2647E1800B17809504600D01839F13FEF57E647609B8C4A79B24C924B5281A01AE321606B1B820DC951A11470058B222400E5017E2144B5083D2617A97"
    roleAttributes:
      - managed-devices
```

## Settings: `spec.forProvider`

| Field | Type | Default | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|------|---------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | string, required |  | `name` | Name of the posture check. |
| `processes` | list of objects, required |  | `processes` | Processes to look for. Ziti identifies a process by its operating system and path, so each pair may be listed once, and their order does not matter. |
| `processes[].osType` | string, required |  | `processes[].osType` | OsType is the operating system the process runs on. One of `Windows`, `WindowsServer`, `Android`, `iOS`, `Linux`, `macOS`. |
| `processes[].path` | string, required |  | `processes[].path` | Path of the executable. |
| `processes[].hashes` | list of strings |  | `processes[].hashes` | Hashes are the SHA-512 hashes the executable may have. Any executable passes if there are none. Ziti keeps them as a set, so their order and duplicates do not matter. |
| `processes[].signerFingerprints` | list of strings |  | `processes[].signerFingerprints` | SignerFingerprints are the SHA-1 fingerprints of the certificates the executable may be signed with. Any signer passes if there are none. Ziti keeps them as a set, so their order and duplicates do not matter. |
| `roleAttributes` | list of strings |  | `roleAttributes` | RoleAttributes are the attributes service policies select the posture check by, as "#attribute". |
| `semantic` | string | `AllOf` | `semantic` | Semantic says whether all of the processes must be running (AllOf) or any one of them (AnyOf). One of `AllOf`, `AnyOf`. |
| `tags` | map of strings |  | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

The provider also sends `typeId: PROCESS_MULTI`.

The settings every managed resource has, such as `spec.providerConfigRef`,
`spec.managementPolicies` and `spec.writeConnectionSecretToRef`, are described
in [Concepts](../concepts.md).

## How it behaves

- `semantic` says whether all of the processes must run (`AllOf`) or any one (`AnyOf`).
- Ziti identifies a process by its operating system and path, and keeps the processes in that order. The API server rejects a pair that is listed twice.
- Hashes and fingerprints are kept as sets, in lower case without separators, as for a [`PostureCheckProcess`](posturecheckprocess.md).
- A posture check does nothing on its own: name it in `postureCheckRoles` of a [`ServicePolicy`](servicepolicy.md), as `@name` or by a role attribute.

## When something goes wrong

- The API server rejects the manifest: `processes` is empty, an `osType` is not one of the listed values, or the same operating system and path are listed twice.

Create, update, drift, deletion in Ziti and deletion of the resource are covered by the end-to-end test, see [Testing](../testing.md).
